stories.title: Onboarding drop-off
stories.direct_answer: I moved seven-day activation from 31 to 44 percent by fixing what happened after signup, not the emails.
stories.context: Seven-day activation at Fernhill had been flat for two quarters. Everyone assumed the welcome emails were the problem.
stories.approach: I traced the funnel and saw people opened and clicked the emails, then stalled on the bank-linking screen. I decided the fix was the handoff from email to that screen, and I chose seven-day activation as the number to prove it.
stories.action: I rebuilt the trigger so the email fired when someone stalled on that step instead of on day two. I worked with the product designer to cut the bank-linking screen from three steps to one.
stories.ownership: I owned the diagnosis, the trigger rebuild and the metric. The product designer owned the screen redesign.
stories.result: Within a quarter, seven-day activation went from 31 to 44 percent.

branches.trigger: How did you know it was the bank-linking step?
branches.angle: Funnel by step showed clicks held but completion of bank linking dropped.
The first trigger fired too fast and annoyed people mid-flow; moved it to 20 minutes after stalling.

methods.spoken: Whenever a number stalls, the first thing I do is find where people actually drop before I change anything.
